_comment: Static security controls applied to every Databricks cluster policy.
This file is the source of truth for the settings that must not vary by
domain or environment. terraform/modules/databricks-compute merges it with
the dynamic parts — cost-attribution tags, the node-type allowlist and the
Kept as JSON rather than HCL so it can be reviewed and tested without
Terraform: scripts/python/validate_policies.py asserts that every control
below is still present and still fixed, which is a check that runs in CI on

data_security_mode._why: Unity Catalog row filters and column masks only apply in this access mode. A cluster in a weaker mode reads the underlying files and bypasses them entirely.

spark_version._why: An LTS runtime. A platform that tracks the newest runtime spends its time debugging the newest runtime.

runtime_engine._why: Usually cheaper per query despite the higher DBU rate, because it finishes sooner. Left unlocked rather than fixed — it is a loss on small non-vectorisable jobs.

azure_attributes.first_on_demand._why: The driver stays on-demand. An evicted driver fails the whole run and loses every completed task; an evicted worker loses one task.

cluster_log_conf.path._why: Cluster logs must land somewhere durable, or a failed job's stderr dies with the cluster.

enable_local_disk_encryption._why: Encrypts the temporary local storage Spark spills shuffle data to. That spill contains real customer data.
